title: Sign in
purpose: Start a session using the account issued by your laboratory.
summary: Sign in with the account your laboratory issued. Staff and client accounts use this same page.

tasks.title: Sign in with your password
steps: Type your username or email in [[Login]] and your [[Password]].
Check [[Remember me]] to stay signed in after closing the browser.
Select [[Sign in]]. If you have an authenticator app, you are asked for its code next; if the laboratory requires one you have not set up, you set it up next.

tasks.title: Sign in with an emailed code
steps: Select [[Email me a sign-in code]] and enter the email on your account.
Type the code from the email in the same browser within five minutes.

tasks.title: Recover a forgotten password
steps: Select [[Forgot your password?]] and follow the recovery instructions.

good_to_know: Accounts are issued by the laboratory. There is no public sign-up.
Notices beside the form come from the laboratory and are the same for everyone who opens this page.
Failed attempts are rate limited. Signing in never adds roles or access to another client's records.
The administration site has no separate sign-in: it uses this page and the same second factor.
After an automatic sign-out the page says why, and signing in again returns you to the page you were on.

sections.title: Announcements
paragraphs: Notices from the laboratory can appear in a box beside the sign-in form on wide screens, or under it on narrower ones, newest first, each marked Notice or Important with a title and a plain-text message. They are shown to anyone who opens this page, before signing in, so they never depend on your account. The laboratory’s administrators post and withdraw them; nothing appears when none is current. Staff and client users may see further announcements after signing in, on the dashboard or the client portal home page.

Beside the form, the box is always the same height as the form. When the notices are longer, scroll inside the box with the mouse or trackpad, or press Tab after the Sign in button to reach the box and use the arrow keys. Under the form the box shows all of its text.
A public demonstration may list shared accounts and their password in an announcement here. Those accounts cannot change their password, email addresses or two-factor settings after signing in.

items.label: Login
items.description: Required username or email address, as the placeholder Username or email explains. After a refused sign-in the page shows again what was typed here, so a typo can be corrected; do not type a password in this field. Staff and client accounts use this same page; their account assignment controls the destination and records they can access.

items.label: Password
items.description: Required account password. Use Forgot your password?, on the row under this field beside Remember me, for the email-based recovery form. When outgoing email is off, recovery instructions direct you to the laboratory administrator.

items.label: Remember me
items.description: Optional, initially unchecked. Checked keeps the session cookie after the browser closes, for up to 24 hours after the session was last saved; unchecked ends the cookie when the browser session ends. Either way your laboratory's session limits sign you out after a period without activity and after the longest session, counted from sign-in.

items.label: Sign in
items.description: Checks credentials and active account status, then asks for an enrolled second factor when applicable. A valid next destination takes precedence; otherwise sign-in goes to the dashboard, which routes client users to their portal.

items.label: Email me a sign-in code
items.description: Opens the email-code request page as an alternative to entering your password. Enter the email on your laboratory account there, then type the emailed code in the requesting browser within five minutes. This action appears when the deployment uses an email backend other than the disabled dummy backend. Its availability does not confirm successful email delivery. An enrolled second factor is still required when applicable.

sections.title: Enabled behavior
paragraphs: Public sign-up is closed; the laboratory issues accounts through administration. Username/email password login is enabled and does not require an email code. Passkey login is not offered. Password sign-in permits unverified email, but that does not establish email ownership or satisfy MFA enrollment prerequisites. A successful email-code sign-in verifies the account email. Failed attempts are rate limited. A successful login never adds laboratory roles or access to another client’s records. No invitations are sent by this screen.

The administration site has no separate sign-in. Opening it while signed out leads here, so the same failed-attempt limit and enrolled second factor apply, and afterwards returns to the administration page that was requested. An account without Staff status that is already signed in is refused there.

An administrator can require a second sign-in factor of chosen accounts on Security settings. An account the rule covers that has no authenticator app is sent to Set up a second sign-in factor after signing in, by password or emailed code, and opens nothing else until it adds one; Continue then goes on to the page the sign-in was opening.

A superuser can mark an account's password as compromised in the admin console. That password then no longer signs the account in on its own: a sign-in with it alone is signed out at once, and this page says what to do. A sign-in that also gives the account's authenticator code, or an emailed sign-in code, opens only Choose a new password until a new one is saved, after Set up a second sign-in factor where the laboratory requires one and the account has none. Forgot your password? sets a new one and lifts the mark too.

sections.title: Sign-in activity
paragraphs: Completed sign-ins, rejected passwords (including rate-limited attempts), rejected sign-in codes and explicit sign-outs are recorded in the deployment’s application logs. A completed sign-in is recorded only after the account's enrolled second factor, if it has one, succeeds. For an account the laboratory requires a second factor of that has none yet, the entry records the password or code sign-in; the session then opens only the setup pages until an authenticator app is added, and the log does not record that step. The log names a stored account by username when it can identify one; unknown or ambiguous login text is recorded as unknown. Passwords and codes are never included. These operational logs follow the deployment’s log retention and survive database resets; they are separate from laboratory record audit history.
